subject: creating a Coverage layer for DSM

messages.author: da60e261c0fc5224
messages.subject: creating a Coverage layer for DSM
parts:
Hello,

Just wondering if someone can help me with importing GIS information
into Distance 6.0. When I attempt to create a Coverage layer (for
Density Surface Modelling) I receive a message which says "The new layer
will have approximately 0 grid points in it, Do you want to continue?".
If I click "yes", I receive a message saying that "No grid points fell
inside the survey area".=20

I have checked to see if the grid points fall within the survey area,
and according to ArcGIS 9.2 they do. I have checked that the coordinate
system is the same as the global coordinate system, and they are (and I
switched the global coordinate system off within Distance before
attempting to create the Coverage layer). Any ideas or pointers would be
very helpful!

Many thanks in advance!

Chandra Salgado

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: creating a Coverage layer for DSM
parts:
Chandra:

Look at the Properties associated by default with the Coverage layer you
are trying to create. There will be a default spacing of the grid
points. Distance is reporting that the spacing is too coarse for any
points to fit within the specified (by the shape file) study region
boundary.

Specifying the spacing is an iterative process in Distance; recall you
are essentially going to overwrite the coverage layer that you are
asking Distance to manufacture by the prediction grid that you have
constructed with your GIS. If my advice confuses you even further, send
your project along to me, and I can have a look next week (after we
finish our workshops here in St. Andrews).
